headline: Adopted prior meeting minutes; discussed Weed Warriors volunteers, the Green Community Festival, and parks and open space goals.
summary: The committee discussed a possible volunteer effort to remove invasive plants from city parks, including replanting. Members also reviewed festival booth plans and parks and open space goals from City Plan 2024. The only recorded vote was to adopt the minutes of the previous meeting.
decisions: Adopted the August 05, 2026 meeting minutes unanimously, with Ms Balerna and Ms Wikle abstaining.

decision_evidence.quote: Mr Bossange motioned to adopt, Ms Yankowski 2nd. Adopted unanimously. Ms Balerna and Ms Wikle abstained.

plain_text:
NATURAL RESOURCES & CONSERV ATION COMMITTEE 
Meeting Minutes 
September 02, 2026 
 
The South Burlington NRCC held it's regular monthly meeting for September 02, 2026, at 6:00 pm, in 
room 301 at the South Burlington City Hall, 180 Market St, and by GoToMeeting for remote 
participation. 
 
Attending: J Balerna (Chr); J. Bossange (Vice Chr); L. Yankowski; K. Boyk; M. Huth;  S. Comeau; J 
Wikle 
 
Also attending:  S. Kershner (City Liaison);  R. Doyle 
 
1. Ms Balerna welcomed everyone. 
2. No changes, deletions or additions to the agenda. 
3. Meeting minutes from  August 05, 2026. 
1. Mr Bossange motioned to adopt, Ms Yankowski 2nd.  Adopted unanimously. Ms Balerna and 
Ms Wikle abstained. 
4. Comments from the public:  Mr Doyle mentioned Weed Warriors and what is involved with 
trying to organize volunteers to continue removal/eradication/control of invasive plants in the 
city parks. How about replanting projects.  Various committee members mentioned the history 
and work of Weed Warriors.  We will need to investigate trying g to move something like this 
forward.  The gentleman who was hired by the city and who ran Weed Warriors had trained 
volunteers what to look for and do. 
5. Green Community Festival Sept 19 
1. Ms Yankowski will staff our booth all day, Ms Balerna, Mr Bossange, Ms Boyk & Ms Huth 
will be covering various hours throughout the event.  Ms Balerna has the information for the 
Rewilding Project. We have a banner and various materials for our table. 
6. Working group updates. 
1. We need to work on Human-Wildlife interactions. 
2. Ms Boyk said the Parks & Open Space Management Plan group had met.  CivicSol shared 
the data they've been compiling. City Plan 2024 has the following goals related to 
parks and open space: 
     1. 7.5 acres of developed recreation per 1,000 population 
               2. 20 acres of natural recreation per 1,000 population 
               3. Recreational amenity within 1/4 mile of every residential dwelling unit 
               4. Protect 51% of the city's land area as open space 
       Goals 1 and 2 are currently met but will fall short based on projected 2050          
 population, so the plan will likely recommend adding some parks and natural areas as 
 the population grows. Goal 3 is not currently met in several parts of the city so the plan 
 will recommend adding recreation areas or improving access in certain neighborhoods. 
 CivicSol is still finalizing data for goal 4 but they think we are close to 51%. 
  However,  Ms Boyk is unsure about some of the land types or protection types    
  that are being included in this measurement and hopes to receive more detailed 
  data and a map before the plan is finalized. 
3. Mr Bossange will update us on what the Land Trust has involved with, including the Long 
Property.
We adjourned at 6:53pm           Our next meeting is October 07, 2026  at 6:00pm 
 
Next agenda items: 
– how the Green Community Festival went 
– Land Trust Updates. 
– Rewilding
